'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Mali War]]
**[[Battle of Tinzaouaten (2024)|Battle of Tinzaouaten]]
***The [[Wagner Group]] states that it and the [[Malian Armed Forces|Malian military]] sustained heavy losses in clashes with [[Tuareg]] rebels near the [[Algeria–Mali border]]. [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/world/2024/07/29/russia-s-wagner-says-it-took-losses-in-heavy-fighting-against-rebels-in-mali- (Al Arabiya)] [https://www.france24.com/en/africa/20240729-russia-s-wagner-group-reports-casualties-in-intense-clash-with-tuareg-rebels-in-mali (France 24)]
***The [[Main Directorate of Intelligence (Ukraine)|Main Directorate of Intelligence of Ukraine]] claims that it provided assistance to the Tuareg rebels in their battle against Wagner Group mercenaries in [[Mali]]. [https://amp.theguardian.com/world/article/2024/jul/29/ukraine-military-intelligence-claims-involvement-in-deadly-wagner-ambush-in-mali (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Eastern Ukraine campaign]]
***[[Ukrainian Ground Forces|Ukrainian army]] sergeant Oleh Chaus reports that the [[Russian Ground Forces|Russian army]] captured the eastern [[Donetsk]] villages of [[Prohres]] and Vovche, citing [[List of military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War|insufficient weapon supplies]], [[NATO Security Assistance and Training for Ukraine|deficient training]], and decreased motivation as causes of the setback. [https://apnews.com/article/russia-ukraine-war-drone-attack-pokrovsk-94081120780d30f9d2ecbfd32257c42e (AP)]
*[[2024 France railway arson attacks]]
**[[National Police (France)|French police]] arrest a [[far-left extremist]] who may have been behind an attack on the [[TGV]] long-distance train network ahead of the opening of the [[2024 Summer Olympics]] in [[Paris]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/french-police-arrest-far-left-suspect-after-rail-sabotage/a-69794459 (DW)]
*[[2024 Iran–Israel conflict]], [[Israel–Hezbollah conflict (2023–present)|Israel–Hezbollah conflict]]
**A Hezbollah militant and a [[Redwan force|Redwan commando]] are killed and three injured in an IDF strike in Lebanon.[https://apnews.com/article/israel-hamas-war-latest-29-july-2024-1213b56409f36211815020ea0fdfee28 (AP News)]
**Major international flagship airlines including [[Lufthansa]], [[Turkish Airlines]], and [[Ethiopian Airlines]] cancel or delay flights at [[Beirut–Rafic Hariri International Airport]] in [[Lebanon]] due to threats of [[Israel]]i retaliation towards [[Hezbollah]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2024/7/29/lebanons-beirut-airport-cancels-flights-over-fears-of-israeli-attack (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Human Rights Watch]] reports widespread acts of sexual violence in the [[Sudan]]ese capital of [[Khartoum]], including [[gang rape]] and [[forced marriage]]s committed by [[Sudanese Armed Forces|the army]] and [[Rapid Support Forces]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/sexual-violence-widespread-sudans-capital-report-says-2024-07-29/ (Reuters)]
*Protesters taking part in a march in [[Gwadar]], [[Pakistan]], attack security forces deployed to guard them, killing a soldier and injuring 16 others, according to the [[Pakistani Army]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/pakistan-army-says-protesters-kill-soldier-injure-16-2024-07-29/ (Reuters)]
*[[Far-right politics in Israel|Far-right]] [[Israel]]i protestors, including several members of the [[Knesset]], storm the [[Sde Teiman detention camp]] after military police from the [[Israel Defense Forces|defense forces]] detained nine [[reserve duty (Israel)|reservists]] on suspicion of sexually abusing a [[Palestinian]] detainee. [https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/2024-07-29/ty-article/.premium/idf-police-raid-sde-teiman-prison-detain-soldiers-suspected-of-abusing-detainee/00000190-fe2c-d22a-abfe-ff2c10c20000 (''Haaretz'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*The [[United Arab Emirates]] grants [[lottery]] licenses for the first time in the country's history. [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/gulf/2024/07/29/uae-grants-firm-lottery-license-for-first-time-in-potential-move-towards-casinos- (Al Arabiya)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*At least two people are killed and as many as 100 others are injured when a passenger train carrying 800 people collides with a [[Kamaz]] truck near [[Volgograd]], [[Russia]], and partially derails. [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/world/2024/07/29/two-dead-up-to-100-injured-after-russian-train-and-truck-collide- (Al Arabiya)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Guatemala–Mexico relations]], [[Mexican drug war]]
**The [[Guatemalan government]] grants [[temporary resident]] permits to over 200 [[Mexicans]], mostly children, on [[humanitarian]] grounds as they escape drug violence. [https://apnews.com/article/guatemala-mexico-refugees-cartels-violence-b4a0d0f16ab9308a6505ca3c67911676 (AP)]
*[[Panama–Venezuela relations]], [[2024 Venezuelan presidential election]]
**[[Panama]] suspends diplomatic relations with [[Venezuela]] and withdraws its [[diplomat|diplomatic personnel]] from the country until a full review of the presidential election results is concluded. [https://www.reuters.com/world/india/several-feared-dead-after-landslides-indias-kerala-local-media-report-2024-07-30/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2024 Southport stabbing]]
**Three children are killed and ten other people are injured in a [[mass stabbing]] at a dance school in [[Southport]], [[Merseyside]], [[England]]. A teenager is subsequently arrested. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/cevwgqz0x41t (BBC News)]
*Sakina Muhammad Jan becomes the first person to be jailed under [[Australia]]'s [[forced marriage]] laws after ordering her 21-year-old daughter to marry a man who later murdered her. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cx72ll7460vo (BBC News)]
*The [[Grand National Assembly of Turkey]] approves a law ordering the euthanization of stray dogs that are sick or have been deemed aggressive. [https://www.scmp.com/news/world/europe/article/3272347/turkey-approves-controversial-stray-dog-cull (''SCMP'')]
*[[Law enforcement in France|French police]] report multiple sabotage acts targeting telecommunications operators in parts of [[France|the country]], affecting 11,000 clients, with the incidents being treated as [[vandalism]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/france-telecom-fiber-optic-networks-sabotaged/a-69795351 (DW)] [https://www.politico.eu/article/french-fiber-optic-cable-hit-with-alleged-acts-of-sabotage/ (Politico)]
*[[King of Morocco|King]] [[Mohammed VI of Morocco]] [[pardon]]s jailed journalists [[Taoufik Bouachrine]], [[Omar Radi]], and [[Soulaimane Raissouni]], along with 2,476 other convicts, as part of a gesture marking the 25th anniversary of his reign. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/morocco-releases-jailed-journalists-pardons-2476-convicts-2024-07-29/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2024 Venezuelan presidential election]]
**[[Foreign relations of Venezuela]]
***[[United States–Venezuela relations]]
****[[United States]] [[United States Secretary of State|Secretary of State]] [[Antony Blinken]] states that the [[Federal government of the United States|U.S. government]] has "serious concerns" that the [[Venezuela]]n election results do not reflect "the will nor the votes of the [[Venezuelans|Venezuelan people]]" and demands that [[National Electoral Council (Venezuela)|Venezuelan electoral authorities]] publish fair and transparent election results, adding that the United States and the [[International community|international community]] will "respond accordingly". [https://apnews.com/article/us-venezuela-blinken-dd01f952543c1b6ba9d243393202682f (AP)]
***Venezuela recalls its diplomats in [[Argentina]], [[Chile]], [[Costa Rica]], [[Dominican Republic]], [[Panama]], [[Peru]], and [[Uruguay]] after those countries oppose the election results. [https://www.trtworld.com/americas/venezuela-to-pull-envoys-from-seven-countries-after-protests-to-maduro-win-18189254 (TRT World)]
**[[2024 Venezuelan protests]]
***At least one person is killed as protests occur throughout Venezuela due to the disputed election results. [https://apnews.com/article/venezuela-presidential-election-maduro-machado-edmundo-results-acee6c8cd3a8fc88086c2dd71963b759 (AP)] [https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/one-dead-in-venezuela-as-protesters-teargassed-in-wake-of-disputed-vote-101722309979909.html (''Hindustan Times'')]
*[[2024 Serbian environmental protests]], [[Jadar mine|Jadar mining project]]
**Thousands of [[Environmentalist|environmentalists]] and opposition group members protest across [[Serbia]] against a [[European Union]]–[[Government of Serbia|Serbian government]] [[Lithium|lithium mining]] project meant to reduce its dependency on [[China|Chinese]] lithium that would seize and raze several rivers and forests. [https://apnews.com/article/serbia-protest-lithium-excavation-environment-175fd1eab486736b572b0ecbc8567783 (AP)]

***Olympic organisers cancel the second session of triathlon training due to water quality concerns in the [[Seine]] river. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20240729-olympic-organisers-cancel-second-day-of-triathlon-training-in-seine-over-pollution (France 24)]
